## For review: three things to check in the generated Stan

Everything below comes out of `stanControl(run = FALSE)`, which builds the
program and its data list **without compiling or sampling** -- so any of
these is a few seconds to reproduce and read for yourself.

::: {.smaller}
1. **IOV** -- does `iov.x ~ v | OCC` expand into the model you would have
   written by hand?
2. **Mixtures** -- is the eta prior in the right place relative to the
   `log_sum_exp`?
3. **The two eta parameterizations** -- do `"noncentered"` and `"centered"`
   really target the same posterior?
:::

::: rule
:::

::: {.notes}
Before the thank you slide, this is the part I actually want from this
room.

Everything I am about to show comes out of stan control with run equals
false, which builds the Stan program and its data list without compiling
or sampling anything. So each of these takes a few seconds to reproduce,
and you can read the generated program yourself.

There are three places where I want a second opinion. I-O-V. Mixtures.
And the two eta parameterizations.

:::

## IOV: `prior(iov.cl)`?

```stan
parameters {
  real<lower=0> iov_cl;               // estimated magnitude, on the sd scale
  matrix[N, 1] z_rx_iov_cl_1;         // occasion 1
  matrix[N, 1] z_rx_iov_cl_2;         // occasion 2
}
transformed parameters {
  matrix[1,1] L_rx_iov_cl_1 = [[1]];  // unit variance, FIXED
  eta[, 4:4] = z_rx_iov_cl_1 * L_rx_iov_cl_1';
}
model {
  to_vector(z_rx_iov_cl_1) ~ std_normal();
  iov_cl ~ cauchy(0, 1);              // <-- the declared prior(iov.cl)
}
```

::: {.smaller}
Is the per-occasion structure the one you would write by hand;
`prior(iov.cl)` describes the **sd** (the `iovXform` scale), not the variance
-- right convention?; and with no prior declared the magnitude is left
**flat and improper** (warned, not substituted) while omega diagonals get a
default half-Cauchy -- should it get one too?
:::

::: {.notes}
Each occasion gets its own eta with a fixed unit variance and those
are scaled by an estimated magnitude theta, here called I-O-V
underscore C-L.

Three things I would still like checked. First, is the per occasion structure
what you would have written by hand?

Second, the magnitude is on the standard deviation scale by default,
is that the convention you would expect?

And third, if you declare no prior at all, the magnitude is now left flat and
improper. It does warn you.

In contrast, the omega diagonals get a default in that situation.

Should an I-O-V magnitude get a default too, and if so, which one?
:::

## Mixtures: is the eta prior on the right side of the `log_sum_exp`?

```stan
matrix[2*N, 1] eta;                    // component-major: 1..N, then N+1..2N
...
to_vector(z_eta_cl) ~ std_normal();    // BOTH components, OUTSIDE the mixture
...
for (i in 1:N)
  sumLL += log_sum_exp(log(p1)    + llCond[i],
                       log1p(-p1) + llCond[N + i]);
```

::: {.smaller}
The claim is that the component-specific etas' priors factor out of the
marginalization, so only the conditionals go inside. **Is that the
marginal you want** -- both components' etas carry a prior whether or not
the subject is in that component? Also: `p1` is passed into `theta` even
though the conditional is asserted to be p-free, and the per-subject
`logLikSubj` used for LOO is the *marginalized* value.
:::

::: {.notes}
Second: mixtures. Two components only, for now.

Here is what I want checked. The eta priors sit OUTSIDE the log sum exp.

Does that marginal make sense given that both components' etas carry
a prior whether or not the subject belongs to that component?

:::

## Two eta styles: do these target the same posterior?

:::: {.columns .codecols}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**`etaParam = "noncentered"`** (default)

```stan
matrix[N, 1] z_eta_cl;

eta[, 2:2] = z_eta_cl * L_eta_cl';

to_vector(z_eta_cl) ~ std_normal();
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**`etaParam = "centered"`**

```stan
matrix[N, 1] etaP_eta_cl;

eta[, 2:2] = etaP_eta_cl;

for (i in 1:N)
  etaP_eta_cl[i] ~
    multi_normal_cholesky(rep_vector(0, 1), L_eta_cl);
```
:::
::::

::: {.smaller}
Both hand the same `eta` matrix to the external conditional, so neither
needs a Jacobian on our side -- Stan owns the whole eta prior either way.
**Is that reasoning right, and would you expect the two to agree to within
MCSE on a real hierarchical PK posterior** (as opposed to just in
principle)?
:::

::: {.notes}
Third: the two eta parameterizations.

On the left, the default, non centered. Is it correct?

On the right, centered. Is it correct?

Stan owns the entire eta prior in both cases.

So: is that reasoning right? And would you expect these two to agree to
within Monte Carlo standard error on a real hierarchical P-K posterior,
rather than just in principle?

:::
